chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Umrat al-Tamattu', then stood at Arafat and stood at Al-Mash'ar, and threw the Jamarah, and sacrificed, and shaved [his head]. Should he cover his head? He said, 'No, until he performs Tawaf with the House, and [Tawaf] with As-Safa and Al-Marwah.' It was said to him, 'And if he did [shave before Tawaf]?' He said, 'I do not see any blame upon him.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةُ: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.الْمَشْعَرُ: Al-Mash'ar (Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the standing place at Muzdalifah)
key_terms.رَمَى الْجَمْرَةَ: Throwing the Jamarah (casting pebbles at the pillars in Mina)
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat (the main standing place during Hajj)
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ التَّمَتُّعِ: Umrat al-Tamattu' (Umrah performed with a separate Hajj, where the pilgrim remains in Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on covering the head and the validity of shaving before completing Tawaf for Umrat al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the sequence of rites for Umrat al-Tamattu', emphasizing that the prohibition against covering the head (Ihram restriction) persists until the completion of the Umrah-specific Tawaf and Sa'i, even if other Hajj rites are finished. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of Umrah's concluding rituals within the broader Hajj framework, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the order of obligations. The Imam's leniency if the act was already performed highlights the distinction between mandatory sequence and compensatory penalty.
